reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Excellent evidence - complete suppression of free C5 from 172.7 μg/mL to 0.0 μg/mL at all timepoints demonstrates robust target engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Strong evidence - hemolysis reduction from 105.8% to <2% confirms downstream complement pathway inhibition as expected. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Clear success - primary endpoint met with clinically meaningful -5.8 point reduction in QMG score (p=0.0004), well above the 3-point MCID for QMG. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Good response rate with 70% achieving ≥5-point QMG reduction, suggesting broad efficacy in this refractory pediatric MG population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design limits interpretation, but very small sample size (n=12) and strong effect size with low p-value support genuine efficacy despite design limitations.

failure_modes.evidence: Very small sample size of 12 participants limits statistical power and generalizability, though strong effect size partially mitigates this concern
